photos.c: Above: Stephen Sharp (stage 6), Phil Wicks (2), Jonathan Blackledge (5), Spencer Barden (4), Alaster Stewart (1) and Tim Watson (3) receive the Ian Logan Trophy – Belgrave’s fourth year of being top of the pile at Rushmoor Arena.  Only Stephen and Jonathan remained in the squad from 2004’s winning line-up.
“Sweatshop” Surrey CC League Race 1 at Brockwell Park, and Phil Wicks (9) and Stephen Sharp (1) slug it out at the front of the field.
With “Sweatshop” Surrey Cross Country League race less than one minute old, Phil Wicks has made clear his intentions.  He went on to claim his first league win.  Photo by Steve Wicks.
Phil Wicks laid his cards on the table at Lloyd Park, pushing on hard from the start, but it was Thames Hare & Hounds’ John McFarlane (263) who held all the aces.

Above: The start of the Eastleigh 10k on March 19th.  The race included the CAU Inter-Counties Championship and Belgravians were racing in some unfamiliar vests.  In the red vest with white/red shorts towards the left is the eventual race winner Angus Maclean (Team Southampton). 31 is Richard Ward (Belgrave/Surrey), 32 Phil Wicks (Belgrave/Surrey), between and just behind  these latter two is Tim Watson in a white/green vest (Belgrave/Hampshire).  To the right of Phil is Hassan Raidi (Belgrave/Surrey), Jonathan Blackledge (Belgrave), and 15 Jermain Mays (Kent AC/Kent).  Maclean's winning time was 29:47, Mays was second in 30:00 and Phil Wicks 3rd in 30:02.  Belgrave won the team race and Surrey the Inter-County Championship. Full result and report in the previous issue.  Photo by Steve Wicks.

Above: Start of the South of Thames Championship in Brockwell Park: Dave Anderson, Pete Willis (20), Mike Trees (18), James McMullen (Epsom Oddballs 142), Will Clark (Epsom & Ewell 137), Alan Barnes (Herne Hill 175), James Connor (Kent AC), Phil Wicks (19), Dean Lacy (Cambridge H 51), Alex Bodin.

Above: A mile gone in the men’s race and Barry Royden (847 Medway & Maidstone) holds a narrow lead with Matt Ashton (3 Aldershot F&D), Darren Deed (61 Bedford &C) and Phil Wicks (100 Belgrave) in echelon. Just behind Royden is Huw Lobb (Bedford), Dominic Bannister (Shaftesbury) and Andy Robinson (Newham & Essex Beagles).

Happy with a seventh successive year in the medals at the National Road Relay. Standing (left to right) Gerry North, Gordon Biscoe, Bill Laws, Brian Pritchard, Tom Osment, Maureen Pritchard, Zara Chidoub, Mark Pollard, Jonathan Blackledge, Janet Blackledge, Mike Blackledge, Neil Speaight, Alan Mead, Padraic Buckley, Paul Freary, Eric Hall, Pete Willis, Hazel Mead.
